title: Context filter
evidenceStatus: Five authored search records shared by context; 65 judgments over six documents; no downstream reader trials; offline 101-position and actual-callback probes
summary: The allowance slider changes retained-card styling but never the live model input: zero retained sources still sends all six documents and displays the full-context choice. Recorded and live filtering policies also differ, and late responses replace newly selected examples. Build a versioned token-budget selector plus a separately scored downstream reader before claiming useful context reduction.
strengths: Visible document text and stable source IDs make selection inspectable.
Recorded cases correctly preserve all four labeled positive sources and abstain on the one absent-answer case.
The UI explicitly states that downstream reduced-context success is not measured.
The recording note correctly describes filtering as a heuristic rather than a security boundary.

findings.title: The allowance changes a preview without changing evaluation inputs
findings.evidence: src/agent-experiments.tsx:139 uses kept only for styling; line 234 always sends all documents. Actual callbacks at 0% retain nothing but send six documents and show refund. The line-466 inspector omits budget/current subset and can export the original kept list.
findings.impact: The displayed answer and saved state do not establish any outcome from reduced context, despite the useful disclaimer.
findings.fix: Separate selector and reader results; send the exact inspected subset to a fixed reader and bind answer/citations/export to source/query/budget hashes.

findings.title: Live filtering omits recorded policy decisions
findings.evidence: compositions.py:202 retains relevant low-injection or host-critical records. src/agent-experiments.tsx:233 asks seven questions versus thirteen recorded, omitting injection judgments. A synthetic relevance .98/injection .99 source is retained by UI but excluded by the recorded rule.
findings.impact: Recorded filtering outcomes do not validate the live policy or the critical-record behavior. The synthetic mismatch is not an observed live compromise.
findings.fix: Share a versioned policy, keep host-mandatory retention explicit, and separate untrusted source data from executable instructions without treating model scores as an authorization boundary.

findings.title: Source-slot percentages do not measure useful token-budget tradeoffs
findings.evidence: src/agent-experiments.tsx:144 rounds budget/100 times six, combined with relevance >=.5. All 101 default settings yield only two subsets: empty through 8%, one source from 9% through 100%. Inputs total only 336 characters with one positive source per answerable query.
findings.impact: The demo cannot show token savings or survival of multi-source dependencies, exceptions and critical facts.
findings.fix: Count exact serialized-reader tokens, pack spans/dependency groups under budget, expose infeasible mandatory retention and test independently labeled sufficient-evidence groups.

findings.title: A late response replaces a newly selected example
findings.evidence: src/agent-experiments.tsx:261 accepts any completion. Probe starts refund, selects invoice, then resolves refund: selector/input remain invoice while output and row text become refund.
findings.impact: Selection, visible inputs, output and evidence provenance describe different runs.
findings.fix: Bind results to example/query/corpus/budget revisions; reject stale application and preserve older completed runs only in comparison history.

simulation.title: An evidence tray with measured downstream consequences
simulation.description: Inspect current/outdated policy, a user exception and tool outcomes; pin required facts, lower a token allowance, compare full and reduced reader runs, restore missing evidence and finish with a supported answer or explicit insufficient-evidence result.
simulation.jevsRole: Judge which source spans or dependency groups matter to the query and identify unresolved semantic relevance.
simulation.codeRole: Own source versions, trust metadata, mandatory retention, tokenizer counts, packing, exact reader payloads, revision checks and independent outcome scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: Reader input exactly equals inspected retained context, including at zero budget.
Every quote maps to an immutable source/version without changing negation, numbers or temporal scope.
Mandatory records fit or yield an explicit infeasible-budget state.
Answer support and abstention are checked independently of selector judgments.
Late results cannot attach to another example, query, corpus or budget.
Export contains tokenizer/version, actual prompt, selected spans, raw decisions and full/reduced outcomes.

evaluation.design: Independently label 24 development and 120 held-out 32-chunk bundles across six strata. Two orderings produce 240 presentations. One 64-judgment Jev selection per presentation plus three selectors at two token budgets and one full reader baseline gives 1920 future calls before retries. Use a fixed reader, independent sufficient-evidence groups, exact answer predicates and 10000 paired bundle-clustered bootstrap samples. Optional complete RULER 4K follow-up covers all 13 default tasks with 500 samples each.
baselines: Frozen lexical/BM25 selection with identical host retention and token packing
Pinned local LLMLingua-2 at matched budgets
Independent gold evidence groups as a diagnostic bound
metrics: Independent answer correctness, support and abstention
Exact serialized tokens, infeasible budgets and total selector-plus-reader latency/cost
All-attempt availability, stale-result failures and paired quality/resource curves
Official RULER string-match scoring separately from stricter optional diagnostics

coverage.current: Five shared search fixtures, 65 judgments, six documents/336 characters, 4/4 positive evidence retention and 1/1 abstention. Zero downstream runs and zero external benchmark cases.
coverage.full: Authored plan: 120 held-out bundles times two orders, 240 Jev calls/15,360 selector judgments plus 1,680 reader calls = 1,920. External follow-up: RULER default 13 tasks times 500 = 6,500 samples at a declared 4K length; three selectors/two budgets/full baseline require 45,500 reader calls plus at least 6,500 selection calls = 52,000 before retries or splits.
coverage.feasibility: Authored study is manageable once a fixed reader and token/packing system exist. Full RULER needs pinned generation/scoring/tokenizer, source preparation, local compressor resources and substantial future call budget; longer lengths are separate complete runs. No model calls, datasets or weights were acquired during this audit.

libraries.name: Transformers.js tokenizers
libraries.use: Count the actual reader prompt with its pinned tokenizer/chat template; do not present another model's tokenizer as exact provider accounting.

libraries.name: LLMLingua-2
libraries.use: Provide a local rate-controlled compression baseline, with protected sections where applicable; compare independent reader quality and total cost rather than assuming published gains transfer.

nextSteps.action: Connect retained spans to a separate reader run and export the actual reduced payload.
Share recorded/live selection policy, host retention and revision guards.
Implement exact token accounting and dependency-aware packing.
Build and independently label the complete authored outcome comparison.
Run all 6,500 default RULER cases at 4K after reader, resource and call-budget preparation.
